Charity gig planned to support Ukrainian families

A touring band from northern England is organising a charity concert in aid of families affected by the war in Ukraine.

The group has played in schools, hospitals and rehabilitation centres in Ukraine since the full-scale invasion began.

The concert will be held in Manchester in February and streamed online.

Several well-known artists will appear by video link. It will be promoted by an experienced events organiser, who has worked on large benefit concerts before.

The band's singer said it was "fantastic" to see so many artists support the idea.

"We were motivated by what we saw on our tours of Ukraine."

He said the gig was less about celebrity names and more about "music being a force for good".

"Music can play a powerful role in people's lives, and we're very lucky that everyone has come on board."

The promoter, Mr. Grant, said he was "really pleased" to play a part in the event.

"We must stand together and play a role in pressuring the need to stop this war."

Ukrainian bands will also take to the stage alongside the headline acts.

The singer said: "We saw the destruction up close, but we also saw a culture of joy and a desire to move forward."

Money will be raised for charities supporting children, de-mining and energy resilience for schools.

The charities provide trauma support for women and children, among other services.

A special recording

Ahead of the concert, the band released a recording of a traditional Ukrainian carol with a children's choir.
